stories.headline: Tisza wins historic supermajority: official final count confirms 141 seats, 53% of votes
stories.summary: Hungary's National Election Office confirmed the Tisza Party won 141 of 199 parliamentary seats (53.18%) with record 79.56% turnout in the April 12 election, up from the initial 138-seat projection after postal, overseas mission, and transferred votes were counted. Fidesz-KDNP finished with 52 seats, Mi Hazánk with 6. Tisza flipped three additional constituencies (Paks, Dombóvár, Nyírbátor) after the final count.

stories.headline: Government formation timeline takes shape: May 9 inaugural parliament session, mid-May swearing-in targeted
stories.summary: Following Sulyok formally tasking Magyar with forming a government, the Tisza Party announced a May 9 inaugural parliament session and mid-May cabinet swearing-in target. Magyar pushed for the earliest possible transfer of power, announced Bujdosó Andrea as parliamentary group leader, and said he would name his first seven ministers the following Monday. Both parties and Mi Hazánk held preparatory talks on the parliament's inaugural session.

stories.headline: Magyar demands President Sulyok resign, confrontational meeting at Sándor Palace triggers constitutional questions
stories.summary: PM-elect Magyar called President Sulyok 'unworthy' and 'unfit' during and after their April 15 meeting at Sándor Palace, demanding his resignation following the new government's formation. Sulyok said he was 'considering' the arguments but his former communications director told media he would not step down voluntarily. Legal analysis showed removal would require a complex process involving the Constitutional Court even with a two-thirds majority.

stories.headline: Sulyok signs last-minute appointments before power transfer: Fidesz-aligned university rector, brigadier general dismissal, judges
stories.summary: President Sulyok made several controversial personnel decisions in the days after the election result, signing off on a five-year extension of Fidesz-linked ex-Justice Minister László Trócsányi as rector of Károli Gáspár Reformed University through 2032. He also immediately dismissed Brigadier General Bodó Bernadett at the initiative of outgoing Interior Minister Pintér, and made various judicial appointments/dismissals on the National Judicial Office president's recommendation.

stories.headline: EU-Hungary talks produce agreement to work together on releasing frozen funds; Magyar outlines four-step reform plan
stories.summary: A high-level European Commission delegation led by von der Leyen's chief of staff Björn Seibert held technical meetings in Budapest on April 17–18 with Tisza representatives. Magyar announced a four-step plan centered on anti-corruption, judicial independence, and press freedom. Both sides agreed to work together; the Commission confirmed it was unprecedented for such a senior delegation to meet a party not yet in power. The talks also covered Hungary's block on a €90bn EU loan to Ukraine and the Erasmus/Horizon university dispute.

stories.headline: Magyar announces suspension of state broadcaster, confronts public media in extraordinary live interview
stories.summary: PM-elect Magyar announced plans to suspend the Orbán-era state broadcaster and rebuild it as an independent public service outlet. He appeared in two tense live interviews on state radio and television, accusing presenters of spreading 'lies' and comparing their coverage to Nazi and North Korean propaganda. He said Orbán's allies controlled around 400 media outlets. The announcement drew wide international coverage as a symbol of the 'regime change.'

stories.headline: Magyar's diplomatic sprint: Poland/Tusk first foreign visit, UK/Starmer call, Ukraine stance, Russia 'pragmatic' relations
stories.summary: Magyar announced Warsaw as his first foreign destination to build on Polish PM Donald Tusk's congratulations, citing Poland's experience repairing EU relations as a model. He held a phone call with UK PM Keir Starmer, who thanked him for Ukraine support. On Russia, Magyar said he would answer Putin's calls but not initiate contact, while stating Hungary must honour existing energy contracts; Ukrainian officials interpreted the result as a strategic defeat for Putin. Fico (Slovakia) announced plans to confront Magyar personally over migration allegations.
